15.text: The Koryak and Chukchee form the third group of reindeer-breeders,

16.text: and live to the east and north of the Tungus. Like the tribes of the extreme

17.text: west, they use reindeer only with the sledge, not for riding, and their herds

18.text: are very numerous, perhaps the most numerous in the world; but the degree

19.text: of domestication is very imperfect. One is almost tempted to assume that

20.text: they did not introduce the tame reindeer from their neighbors, but that, in

21.text: imitation of them, they attempted to domesticate the race of reindeer inhabiting

22.text: their own country. This would seem the more plausible, since their reindeer

23.text: is quite different from that of the Tungus. Their dogs are likewise the natural

24.text: foes of the reindeer-herds, and the latter are so wild that they return easily

25.text: to their former freedom. Milking is impossible; and the reindeer are difficult
